2. The Petitioner, by filing this writ Petition, has invoked the jurisdiction of this Court under Article 226 of the Constitution of India in seeking a direction to the Opposite Parties to acquire the land measuring Ac 5.46 decimals owned by him and award compensation in consonance with the provisions contained in the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 in further granting alternative agricultural site as per the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy of the State in place.

sentences.text:
// 2 //
3. Heard Mr. Digambar Mishra, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Mr. Aurovinda Mohanty,
Central Government Counsel for Opposite Party No.1 as also Mrs. Saswata Pattanaik, learned counsel for Opposite Party No.2 to 6.
4.

Keeping in view the submissions made, the averments taken in the petition, counter filed by the Opposite Parties as well as the rejoinder affidavit filed by the Petitioner being gone through with the documents annexed thereto, it is seen that the Petitioner claims to have purchased the agricultural land in question on 07.04.2015.
It is claimed that the entire plot of land has been affected by Brundaban Mishra vs Union Of India & Others ....

sentences.text:
Opposite ... on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46371080/
1 construction of an embankment for Minagadia/Bolaboni Project, and, therefore, it is said that major portion of of the land has been submerged, leaving an area of only Ac 0.36 which itself is unfit for agriculture because of water logging and other impediments.

The case of the Opposite Parties is that the embankment at Minagadia was constructed over the Tulasinulla Bandha way back in the year 2002-03 over the land under plot no.150/198 under Khata No.28/9 of village Belaboni recorded in the name of Minagadia Samasta Gramabasi Tarafa Sabhapati of Minagadia.
But as those lands were not the rayati lands, there was no acquisition, and that the construction was much prior to the purchase of the land by the Petitioner.

It is stated that the Petitioner being a man of the District of Ganjam has purchased the land in question from the recorded tenants knowing fully well that by then since long the lands were lying fallow and // 3 //
unused and the purpose of purchase of the land by the Petitioner was to make money by advancing the claim for acquisition of the said land but not to cultivate and earn which he is now falsely stating.
It is also stated that the Petitioner had never taken possession of the said purchased land nor had possessed the same.

It has also been stated that in course of time, the height of the embankment has been increased by way of renovation done under MGNREGS Scheme of Tulasinulla Bandha Project in the financial year 2016-17 and 2017-18.

entities.text: MGNREGS Scheme of Tulasinulla Bandha Project
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 5. Faced with above rival pleadings when it is found that there arises the disputed questions of facts for being adjudicated in redressing the grievance of the Petitioner as has been advanced for considering the matter of grant of relief as prayed for; we do not find it to be a fit case to entertain the petition so as to exercise the extra ordinary writ jurisdiction.
6. The Writ Petition stands disposed of.
